title: Matrix input and grading
text: A matrix question can ask for one particular matrix, any basis of a space, or any matrix with a stated property. Choose the mathematical test first; the editor collects entries, while the answer test and response tree decide correctness and marks. Try the matrix questions before adapting one.

title: Matrix input and grading
text:
For teachers

Decisions for a question author



What the prompt asks
Appropriate check
Teacher value in the PRT




A particular matrix
AlgEquiv compares dimensions and corresponding entries; EqualComAss also checks written form.
The expected matrix.


Any basis of a null, column or row space
PythonChecker selects basis with JSON space set to nullspace, columnspace or rowspace.
The original matrix \(A\).


Integer entries, a given determinant or nonidentity
Separate PythonChecker nodes select matrix_property with JSON property set to integer_entries, determinant or identity.
The expected property result: true, an exact determinant such as 1, or false.


Another condition, such as Hermitian symmetry or positive definiteness
A named PythonChecker function. Combine conditions in one PRT or give them separate marks in two PRTs.
The value the function needs, such as true for the positive-definiteness examples.



An entry-by-entry check would reject many correct answers to “give any basis” or “give any matrix satisfying these conditions.” See Python answer tests for the choice and the positive-definiteness walkthrough for combined and separately weighted Hermitian-symmetry/positivity rules. The first question requires both; the second awards half for each. The example accepts exact integer or fractional real and imaginary parts, such as 1/2+%i/3. An equivalent native Moodle STACK question needs corresponding Maxima checks; these Python test names are specific to this port.
If the shape is part of the task, let learners choose a bounded number of columns for null or column-space bases, or rows for row-space bases. An empty basis cannot currently be entered because the editor needs positive dimensions. For a fixed-size task, the model answer determines the editor’s shape. The supplied basis and matrix_property functions require exact rational entries (integers or fractions); a custom PythonChecker function can choose another domain within the input limits. Set any partial credit in the response trees; neither correct cells nor green basis vectors earn marks by themselves.


What learners see
A learner fills matrix cells, presses Validate answers to inspect the interpreted matrix, then presses Check answer. Empty cells are invalid. The editor retains typed forms such as x+x or 1/2; resizing keeps cells that still fit and leaves new cells blank. Editing, resizing, resetting or switching variants clears an earlier result and requires validation again. After a basis check, vector colors explain membership and dependence, but the response tree still determines the score.

title: Matrix input and grading
Run STACK question tests
text: Question tests exercise the real STACK grader. XML <qtest> cases and the block’s declarative tests: run for every generated and replayed variant. A failed assertion stops the build and identifies the question and test. Tests also run in CI. See the checker API for the response and result contract.

title: Run STACK question tests
section: Declare the answers and expected result
text:
Declare the answers and expected result
Add tests: to a .stack-question block. Each test needs a unique name, answers and an expectation. Answers may be keyed by XML input name or listed in XML input order. Expressions use the question’s variables; raw("...") submits a literal student string without computing it.
```{.stack-question}
#| label: tested-product
#| file: questions/polynomial-expansion.xml
#| question: Expand a product (form-sensitive)
#| tests:
#|   - name: expanded teacher answer
#|     answers: {ans: 'expand(ta)'}
#|     expect: correct
#|   - name: deliberate wrong answer
#|     answers: {ans: 'raw("0")'}
#|     expect: wrong
#| review: true
```
Use expect: invalid for a deliberately invalid input. Invalid or empty input cannot satisfy an ordinary wrong-answer expectation. Use score: 0.5 or partial: true to assert partial credit. An overall expectation can contain status, score and answer-note, for example:
- name: a particular branch
  answers: {ans: 'raw("0")'}
  expect: {status: wrong, score: 0, answer-note: expected-branch-note}
The answer note must be the actual note produced by the XML branches. For an unambiguous direct-input tree, a named field expectation checks that input’s own tree scores. Use an overall expectation for a tree combining several inputs or for the implicit checker. Tests never substitute a second grader.

title: Run STACK question tests
text:
XML tests and checker tests
XML tests continue to resolve author expressions and compare each named response tree’s score, penalty and answer notes. An XML expected result can name checker when the block has a checker. Declarative tests can test the whole weighted question score, including checker-value.
Use cases that distinguish alternate correct answers, wrong answers, partial credit and the checker’s valid domain. A basis question should test reordered and rescaled bases, dependence, missing vectors and invalid entries. A positive-definiteness question should distinguish Hermitian symmetry from a positive determinant. The supplied examples include XML tests for these properties.

title: Run STACK question tests
text:
Generate, inspect and approve
Generate variants through the shared authoring workflow described in the authoring guide. A candidate must pass its XML tests, declarative tests and full-mark teacher vector before it can be reviewed. Generation failures are authoring errors; failed seeds are not silently skipped. The SymPy backend generates its own seeds. It does not reuse Moodle’s deployed Maxima seeds.
review: true adds Run question tests to the card. In explicit review mode, use it to inspect the frozen plans, including declarative tests. This uses the same grader as the build. A changed checker or grading rule changes the variant’s content identity and requires a fresh approval. Editing test expectations alone does not change that mathematical identity.
Normal course publishing requires approved variants. Teacher previews and review pages may show proposals, which have no published variant number. Do not turn off assertions to publish a failing question.

The extension requires CTM Assessment (with ctm-checkers 0.2.0 or later; 0.3.0 or later forbids learners the names of question and feedback variables, 0.6.0 or later applies STACK’s rules for the text of an answer, below; 0.10.0 or later stops on question options it does not read, applies numerical tests and checkanswertype to answers that are not numbers or not of the teacher’s type, and treats an answer a test cannot decide as false, below), Python 3.9+, SymPy 1.13.3, Quarto 1.8.27+ and HTML output with JavaScript. Set STACK_SYMPY_PYTHON to the Python interpreter to use when Quarto’s default interpreter is not the required environment.


Input and XML reference
The source is a Moodle STACK <quiz> containing named <question type="stack"> entries. Category and description entries are skipped. Retain inputs, PRTs, deployed seeds and <qtest> cases. Unsupported fields and HTML/CASText fail with a question-specific location.



XML input setting
Handling




type
algebraic, scalar numerical, or rectangular matrix.


tans
The input’s model answer. A PRT node’s tans is a separate test argument.


strictsyntax, insertstars
Strict syntax is required. Insertion mode 0 requires explicit *; mode 1 also accepts adjacent products.


forbidwords, forbidfloat
Reject configured words or decimal literals.


requirelowestterms
Reject reducible written integer fractions during validation.


checkanswertype
Refuse an answer of another type than the teacher’s answer (expression, equation, logical expression, list, set or matrix) with a message that names the expected type; a list of the teacher’s length also needs entries of the teacher’s types. This is not a check of the shape or of equality.


mustverify, showvalidation
Verification metadata and preview visibility are retained; this UI always requires validation before grading. Supported visibility values are 0, 1, 3.


syntaxhint, boxsize
Parse the authored hint and size text fields within the supported limits.


matrix
Optional fixed/resizable dimension settings; see matrix input.



allowwords and input options must be empty; nondefault syntax attributes and other insertion modes are unsupported. A question that sets a question option the engine does not read stops the build, with the question’s name, the option and its value: complexno other than i, decimals other than ., scientificnotation other than *10, inversetrig other than cos-1, logicsymbol other than lang, sqrtsign other than 1, multiplicationsign other than dot or none, and matrixparens other than [ or ( (the last two only change how a question writes products and matrices). An absent option is its default. Question-level assumereal and assumepositive affect symbolic assumptions. questionsimplify=0 preserves supported written forms when they survive variant preparation; unsupported held expressions fail clearly.
CASText supports {@expression@} for scalars, collections and matrices, and {@left=right@} for a displayed scalar equality. The placeholders [[input:name]], [[validation:name]] and [[feedback:name]] connect the question text to inputs and response trees. HTML is sanitized. This does not provide arbitrary Maxima evaluation or all STACK text directives.


Answer entry and form
Supported scalar notation includes arithmetic + - * / ^ (also **), parentheses, symbols and STACK’s constants e, pi and Pi, i and %e, %pi, %i; E and I are variables (a current, an energy), as in STACK. PI is a constant in an author’s expressions, but a student writes pi or Pi: PI is rejected as the wrong case (see below). Functions are sqrt, sin, cos, tan, sec, csc, cot, sinh, cosh, tanh, sech, csch, coth, the inverse functions asin, acos, atan, asec, acsc, acot and their hyperbolic forms (asinh, …), exp, log, abs, rational-polynomial gcd and real scalar mod. Aliases are ln, cosec, cosech and STACK’s arcsin, arctan, arsinh, …. mod(x,0)=x follows Maxima’s convention. With insertion mode 1, 2x, 2(x+1) and (x+1)(x-1) are products; xy remains one symbol and spaces alone never imply multiplication.
An answer follows STACK’s rules for its text, with STACK’s messages: a space between two terms is an error (2 x: “Illegal spaces found in expression 2_x.”), and so is a comma outside a list or set (3,5). A name of three letters or more is forbidden (sinx, sin*x: “Forbidden variable or constant: sinx.”) unless STACK knows it (alpha, theta, pi) or it ends in a digit (x1); names are case sensitive (Sin(x): “Input is case sensitive: Sin is an unknown function. Did you mean sin?”; PI: “Input is case sensitive: PI is an unknown variable. Did you mean Pi, pi?”). Unicode letters and symbols that STACK replaces are replaced (π is pi, α is alpha, − is -); other characters are errors (x²). 0^0 is Maxima’s error “expt: undefined: 0^0”. A question test’s inputs are computed as STACK computes them (an input’s name stands for its teacher’s answer, ans1+1 is the teacher’s answer plus 1), and the computed value is then a student’s answer: these rules apply to it, and a test whose input is invalid fails.
Form tests EqualComAss, FacForm, SingleFrac, LowestTerms require a direct input name in sans. EqualComAss preserves structure up to commutative and associative reordering. FacForm requires one polynomial variable in testoptions and handles univariate rational polynomials. SingleFrac checks an equivalent single written fraction or atomic answer. LowestTerms checks written integer fractions and supported denominator restrictions, without comparing the teacher value or cancelling symbolic polynomial factors.
NumAbsolute and NumRelative use the configured tolerance; omitted or syntactically malformed options default to 0.05. NumDecPlaces requires an explicit count from 1 to 50 and checks trailing zeros as written precision. These tests compare finite real numbers. An answer that is not one (a symbol, a complex number, inf, a list, a set, a matrix, an equation) makes the test false, with the message “Your answer should be a floating point number, but is not.” (NumDecPlaces: “Your answer must be a floating point number, but is not.”), and the response tree takes the false branch; NumDecPlaces also needs a decimal literal (1/2 and sqrt(2) are not). A tolerance or a count that is not a number, and a teacher’s answer that is a collection or an equation, are errors of the question. Use a numerical answer test for an approximate measurement rather than treating algebraic equivalence as a tolerance test.


Lists, sets and equations
Lists use [...]; sets use {...}. Both may nest and be empty. Limits are 32 entries per container, six collection levels and 128 total collection nodes, with scalar expression leaves. List comparison is ordered. Set comparison normalizes members without a general proof of every possible scalar identity; see set conventions. Sets explains outer duplicates and missing/extra members. EqualComAss retains list order, nested boundaries and repeated set entries. SameType follows applicability: two sets have the same type, and different-length lists can have the same type. An equation, a logical expression and an expression are three types, so SameType is false for x=1 against x+1. It does not establish equality.
A valid answer that a test does not compare or cannot decide does not stop the grading: the test is false and the response tree takes its false branch. EqualComAss, FacForm and SingleFrac give a message that the answer should be an expression (an equation) for an answer that is not one. For everything else (an answer outside a bound of the test, LowestTerms of a list, an equation or a matrix, a number too large to evaluate) the message is “This answer could not be checked automatically.” and the answer note is the test’s name followed by _undecided. A test that does not exist, an option that is wrong and a teacher’s answer that the test cannot compare remain errors of the question.
Use exact fractions in sets and prepared author collections. Direct decimal list entries have narrower support: literal constant arithmetic with integer powers works; decimal-bearing functions, symbolic terms, transformed collections and transitive author aliases do not. Collection tests require a direct learner input, preserving the literal arithmetic used by the comparison.
AlgEquiv also supports Boolean constants and and, or, not, implies, xor, xnor, with nounand, nounor, nounnot aliases and at most eight Boolean variables. Supported polynomial equations and their disjunctions use a product-of-residuals rule: a=0 or b=0 matches a*b=0. Root multiplicity is retained. Conjunctions/negations of equations, variable denominators and mixtures of equations with Boolean propositions are unsupported. Principal complex roots and logarithms require attention to their domains; the conventions reference records the known differences and proof limits.


Author variables and helpers
Exact arithmetic has a 16,384-bit computation budget for rational numerators and denominators, including intermediate values. Conservative size estimates reject oversized powers before constructing their integers, including arithmetic held for equation and written-form checks. This applies to scalar answers and matrix cells; a custom checker may impose a smaller domain, such as 256-bit rationals.
Write assignments as name:expression;; list indexing is 1-based. In addition to the scalar functions above, authors can use:







Purpose
Supported helpers




Variants
rand, rand_with_step.


Scalar algebra/calculus
diff, expand, factor, ratsimp, cancel, ev(expr), ev(expr,simp), num, denom, integer lcm.


Decimal/significant-figure display
decimalplaces, dispdp, displaydp, significantfigures, dispsf.


Finite collections
set, setify, listify, union, intersection, setdifference, member, subsetp, cardinality.


Model basis generation
nullspace_basis, columnspace_basis, rowspace_basis. The basis checker still receives the original matrix.



ratsimp preserves a supported common-denominator form. listify(list) keeps order; sorting a set with listify supports rational scalar members only. Finite helpers require normal simplification and exact fractions. Prepare their results in question variables before using form-sensitive collection tests; helper feedback variables and held helper execution are unsupported. float is recognized, but floating-point author values cannot be stored in prepared variants and are rejected. Learners cannot call author-only helpers.
Learners cannot use the names of question variables or feedback variables either. An answer such as ta is invalid (“Forbidden variable or constant: ta.”) and shows no preview, so a variable never reveals its value; question tests still use those names. Name a variable so that a learner never needs its name as a symbol: a question variable x would forbid x in every answer.


Policy configuration
Loading definitions with policy-files or page-policy-files does not select a policy. Select project-policy or page-policy explicitly; STACK uses the shared math-exercise policy namespace. This site’s configuration is:
ai-feedback:
  policy-files: feedback/course.yml
  project-policy:
    math-exercise: course-mathematics
A named policy can inherit settings and replace its hint sequence:
ai-feedback:
  policies:
    course-mathematics:
      max-words: 120
      reset-on-run: true
    brief-mathematics:
      extends: course-mathematics
      max-words: 90
    two-step-practice:
      extends: brief-mathematics
      steps:
        - step-prompt: Ask one guiding question without giving a formula or answer.
        - step-prompt: Give a concise worked explanation of this task.
          allow-full-solution: true
Place this definition in a policy YAML file and select feedback-policy: two-step-practice on a card. A stable label targets exercises.math-exercise overrides. The policy resolver applies defaults, project/page selections, exercise overrides, the selected policy and its ancestry, then the current step. steps replaces the inherited list; base-prompt supplies ongoing instructions and step-prompt one step. The retired prompt, inline integrations and inline defaults settings are rejected. See the shared policy reference.
Edits cancel stale responses and clear grading evidence while retaining hint progress. Check resets hints by default; reset-on-run: false preserves progress. Changing variants always resets hints. Only a displayed reply or a generated copy prompt advances the step. .ai-feedback-context and .math-exercise-context are aliases of .ai-context. Explicit jsxgraph:diagram-id references can include visual context through the shared extension; diagrams are not collected implicitly.


Tests, runtime and contribution
PRTs are acyclic response-tree graphs with =, +, - branch score operations, feedback, notes and weighted aggregation. Branch-specific penalties are not supported. Native <qtest> cases check scores, initial-attempt penalty and ordered answer notes, including anchored notes and NULL. The browser has no Moodle attempt state. For custom predicates, also select the checker filename on CLI tests; see the Python guide.
The same Python engine (ctm_checkers.stack) runs locally and in a Pyodide worker. Quarto prepares variants at build time; the worker validates, grades and replays tests. A worker timeout can stop runaway grading. The native comparison and project regression report provide separate evidence, not a blanket compatibility claim. These reports are generated by CI; a normal quarto render does not rerun their mathematical comparisons.
For a source checkout, install requirements-dev.txt and CTM Assessment’s parts at the commits in .github/pins.json, run CTM_COMPONENT_DEV=1 python -m pytest -q tests, and consult the development guide for browser/native checks. Include a minimal XML question and its qtests when reporting a grading issue. General matrix arithmetic, inequalities, units, arbitrary Maxima scripts and Moodle’s full attempt workflow remain unsupported.

For developers

Authored test mismatches
These cases disagree with expectations authored in the XML and are kept out of the interactive gallery. Reviewed causes are named below; an authored-test mismatch alone does not identify whether the cause is the port or the original question. The baseline JSON retains the exact expected and observed results.

AlgMap-8.10
Upstream authoring bug in the PRT. At the failing variant, a=8, b=9, c=2, and d=3, so the correct answer is 8*(t+y)/2 + 9*(t+y)/3 = 7*(t+y). Both authored model answers therefore have no fraction operator. The only full-credit branch requires SingleFrac, which rejects this product; every later branch awards zero. Authored tests 1 and 2 nevertheless expect full credit. The pinned native STACK test also rejects 7*(t+y) under SingleFrac. The port’s random choices expose a latent assumption in the original question; this diagnosis uses the fixed values above, rather than assuming Maxima generates those values for the same seed.

title: Python answer tests and custom checkers
text:
Response and result
The checker receives these values after the selected backend has validated all inputs:







Key
Value




kind
"expressions"


raw
Student strings in XML input order


expressions
Parsed values in the same order


answers
Parsed values keyed by XML input name


teacher
Teacher values keyed by XML input name


variables
Exact question variables


inputs
Named input descriptions, including raw and canonical


variant
{n, id, hash}; an unapproved candidate has no published number


node
Present only during a PythonChecker node call



Matrix input descriptions also carry rows, cols, flattened expressions and a SymPy matrix. symbols maps free symbol names to their SymPy symbols, with the question’s assumptions. The checker namespace contains the shared math-exercise helpers, including SymPy names and assess_basis.
Return True or False, a number between 0 and 1, or a dictionary containing score or correct. Optional keys are feedback, show_score and assessment. Feedback is plain text. A matrix assessment names the input:
return {"score": 0.5, "feedback": "Review the dependent columns.",
        "assessment": {"ans": {"columns": ["correct", "dependent"]}}}
Each assessment list must match the submitted row or column count. A result such as {"valid": False, "feedback": "Enter an integer value."} rejects the attempt without a score. Invalid attempts clear vector assessments. A checker that raises, returns a malformed result or cannot decode a required author value is an author error; it does not count as a wrong learner answer. Each invocation gets a fresh namespace.

title: Python answer tests and custom checkers
text:
Score and placement
A block checker creates an implicit response tree named checker, with checker-value: 1 by default. Its normalized score counts alongside the XML trees:
\[
\text{score}=\frac{\sum_{\text{trees}}\text{value}\times\text{score}}
                       {\sum_{\text{trees}}\text{value}}.
\]
For XML tree scores 1 and 0, both of weight 1, and a checker score 0.5 with checker-value: 2, the question scores 0.5. With no XML trees, the checker supplies the whole grade. Use [[feedback:checker]] in CASText to place its feedback. Penalties and score rounding follow the same rules as XML trees. The name checker is reserved when the block defines a checker.
The XML node and the implicit checker are separate evaluations. A node calls the function as a predicate and supplies response["node"]; the implicit checker call has no node key and contributes its numeric score. Write the function to support both contexts when the XML calls it.

title: Python answer tests and custom checkers
text:
Test and publish
Run XML and declarative question tests for every variant, inspect the student previews, and approve the variants before publishing. Review mode permits proposals for teacher inspection; it does not approve them. Normal publishing requires current approved variants.
